title: eBay pays $46M to journalists it targeted in bizarre harassment campaign
gist: eBay and three former executives agreed to pay nearly $56 million total ($55.7 million in compensation and charitable commitments) to journalists Ina and David Steiner over the 2019 cyberstalking campaign, with eBay paying $46.15 million of it — the headline figure in the title covers only eBay's compensation slice, not the full settlement. Former CEO Devin Wenig personally pays $2 million plus $1 million to charity, and the deal uniquely carried no confidentiality restrictions and forced a public statement condemning the executives and eBay's 2019 culture.

insights.claim: eBay and three former executives agreed to pay nearly $56 million to settle the 2019 cyberstalking campaign against journalists Ina and David Steiner, with $55.7 million in compensation and charitable commitments.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Sets a dollar benchmark for corporate liability in press-harassment cases, far above the criminal penalty the same conduct drew.
insights.locator: eBay and three former executives agreed to pay nearly $56 million

insights.claim: eBay itself pays $46.15 million in compensation to the Steiners plus $6 million to various charities, while the executives' personal contributions are far smaller.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: The corporate entity absorbs roughly 94 percent of the cash, showing individual executive deterrence remains weak.
insights.locator: eBay will pay $46.15 million in compensation

insights.claim: Former eBay CEO Devin Wenig contributes $2 million, former SVP of Global Operations Wendy Jones $500,000, and former Chief Communications Officer Steve Wymer $50,000, plus $1 million from Wenig to a First Amendment charity named for Ina Steiner.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Personal executive liability is now priced but small; D&O coverage and indemnification terms are the thing to check.
insights.locator: The settlement includes another $2 million in compensation

insights.claim: eBay reported $3.1 billion in revenue and $512 million in net income in its most recent quarterly report, making the roughly $52 million of eBay-borne settlement cost about a tenth of one quarter's net income.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Financially immaterial to eBay earnings; the cost here is reputational and precedential, not P&L.
insights.quote: eBay reported $3.1 billion in revenue and $512 million in net income in its most recent quarterly report.
insights.locator: eBay will give $6 million to various charities

insights.claim: eBay previously faced criminal charges and paid a $3 million fine in 2024 under a deferred prosecution agreement with the DOJ, so the civil settlement costs roughly 18 times the criminal penalty.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Civil exposure, not criminal enforcement, is the binding constraint on this class of corporate misconduct.
insights.locator: eBay itself faced criminal charges and agreed to pay a $3 million fine

insights.claim: The main settlement carried no confidentiality restrictions and required eBay to issue a strongly worded public statement about the executives' conduct and the company's 2019 culture.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: A forced public admission with no NDA is a rare term that raises the non-monetary cost of settling such claims.
insights.locator: The main settlement with eBay and former executives did not have any confidentiality restrictions

insights.claim: eBay's required statement condemned the perpetrators and explicitly acknowledged the unprofessional tone in internal communications by Devin Wenig, Steve Wymer and Wendy Jones.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Named-executive acknowledgment in a company statement is unusual and useful precedent for future plaintiffs.
insights.quote: what the Steiners were subjected to by former eBay employees in 2019 was wrong, reprehensible and should never have happened

insights.claim: Settlements were reached with all other eBay employees named in the civil action, and the Steiners filed to withdraw their complaint, ending the case before trial.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Case closure removes the discovery pipeline that had been producing damaging internal eBay communications.
insights.locator: As a result of the settlement, the Steiners yesterday submitted a court filing

insights.claim: The harassment campaign was allegedly spurred in part by an April 2019 article titled eBay CEO Devin Wenig Earns 152 Times That of Employees, showing pay-ratio coverage as the trigger for the executive reaction.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Executive-compensation reporting is a live reputational tripwire; the resulting response created the liability.
insights.quote: eBay CEO Devin Wenig Earns 152 Times That of Employees
insights.locator: The harassment was allegedly spurred in part

insights.claim: An FBI affidavit records then-CEO Devin Wenig telling communications chief Steve Wymer to take Ina Steiner down, and the civil suit alleges both gave employees carte blanche authority to stop her reporting.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: The vague-directive-from-the-top pattern is exactly what converts individual misconduct into corporate liability.
insights.quote: I want to see ashes. As long as it takes. Whatever it takes.
insights.locator: Wenig and Wymer were not charged criminally

insights.claim: The amended complaint describes Wendy Jones asking security executive James Baugh to handle the issue off the radar and saying she did not want to know the details, an explicit plausible-deniability management pattern.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Deliberate-ignorance instructions from executives are now documented liability evidence, not protection.
insights.quote: Just get it done. I don’t want to know the details, just make sure you sync with Wymer.
insights.locator: An amended complaint filed in 2023 described Jones’ alleged role

insights.claim: Devin Wenig maintains the harassment was done in secret without his knowledge, and eBay's 2020 internal investigation concluded his communications were inappropriate but found no evidence he authorized the actions.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: The internal-investigation exoneration did not prevent a personal $3 million payout, showing limited protective value.
insights.quote: harassment was deliberately done in secret and without my knowledge

insights.claim: Seven former eBay employees and contractors pleaded guilty, with prison sentences of 57 months for James Baugh, 24 for David Harville, 18 for Philip Cooke and 12 for Stephanie Popp.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Multi-year prison terms for corporate security staff establish personal criminal exposure for internal investigations gone rogue.
insights.locator: Seven former eBay employees and contractors pleaded guilty

insights.claim: The plaintiffs' lawyer frames the outcome as achieving deterrence of future corporate misconduct and protection for journalists and publishers, positioning it as a landmark civil rights settlement.
insights.speaker: Jon Brodkin
insights.so_what: Expect this settlement to be cited as the anchor number in future corporate-harassment and press-intimidation claims.
insights.locator: Our clients wanted to uncover the truth
